_comment: Verified against this machine on 2026-09-20: PFC3D 6.00 Release 008,
licence 262-082-0013-24092. Do not guess these again.
pfc3d600_console.exe auto-calls the ONE file given as its argument,
but only if the extension is one the command processor recognises.
Hand it a .py and it loads, prints the 'pfc3d>' prompt and waits
forever. It also ignores extra arguments ('exe call foo.py' hangs the
same way) and does not read commands from stdin. So the model script
is run from a one-line .dat wrapper containing
which is how PFC's own shipped examples run Python (see
writes that wrapper when it sees {wrapper} in batch_args.
NOTE: a Python traceback inside PFC does NOT set a non-zero exit
code -- the console still quits 0. The pipeline's check that the
export files exist is the real pass/fail test, not the return code.
